newsitem.title: USA: German president will raise SS pension issue.
newsitem.headline: German president will raise SS pension issue.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog told a U.S. Jewish group on Thursday that he will raise with the German government the issue of Germany's payment of pensions to SS veterans and its failure to pay reparations to East European survivors of the Holocaust.
Herzog made his comments at a meeting with World Jewish Congress President Edgar Bronfman, who described him as "the moral voice of Germany."

A WJC spokesman quoted Herzog as saying he would convey concerns over the payments to the SS veterans and Germany's failure to make reparation payments to residents of former Communist countries, but he cautioned that this was a matter for the German government to deal with.
As president, Herzog said he had limited powers but added that he recognised "the human dimensions" of the problem.
It was revealed last year that Germany was paying disability pensions to hundreds of thousands of SS veterans, including 3,000 who now reside in the United States.
The German government has given the U.S. government a list of SS veterans receiving pensions in the United States.
